34.epoque: The passage is set in the early Christian Church, around 30-33 A.D., a period marked by enthusiasm and rapid growth of the first believers in Jerusalem.
34.passage: This verse is found in chapter 4 of the Acts of the Apostles, which describes the communal life of the early Christians, their unity, and their solidarity in the face of persecution. It illustrates how faith in Christ transformed their relationship with material goods.
34.culture: In the first-century Jewish culture, solidarity and mutual aid were fundamental values. Sharing goods among community members was a common practice, but here it takes on a new dimension with the Christian faith.
34.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of generosity and solidarity within the Christian community. Believers are called to share their resources to ensure that no member suffers from poverty, thus reflecting Christ's love for all.
34.commentaire: This passage reminds us that true Christian community is manifested through love and mutual support. By selling their possessions to help those in need, the early Christians set an example of a living and active faith. We are also called today to evaluate our relationship with material goods and to be ready to share for the good of others, thus reflecting Christ's love in our daily actions.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to deposit' or 'to set aside'. It evokes the idea of entrusting something to another, often in a context of trust or responsibility. In this verse, it emphasizes the act of handing over material goods to the apostles, symbolizing the community's trust in their spiritual leadership. Theologically, this illustrates the principle of the Christian community where resources are shared for the well-being of all.

This term means 'need' or 'necessity'. It indicates a condition of lack or urgent need. In the context of this verse, it underscores the importance of addressing the material needs of community members, which is essential for Christian life. Spiritually, it reminds us of the call to solidarity and mutual aid within the body of Christ.

This word translates to 'distribution' and implies the idea of sharing or allocating resources. It suggests an organized and intentional action to meet the needs of others. In this verse, it highlights how the Christian community ensures that everyone receives what they need, thereby reinforcing the idea of communion and sharing in faith.

35.epoque: This passage is set in the early Christian Church, in a context where believers faced persecution and economic challenges. It was a period of intense spiritual formation and growth, marked by solidarity among community members.
35.passage: In Acts 4, the chapter describes a united Christian community, filled with the Holy Spirit, that shared its resources. Verse 35 illustrates how believers supported one another by laying their goods at the apostles' feet for equitable distribution according to needs.
35.culture: At that time, sharing goods was a common practice in Jewish communities and was reinforced by values of solidarity and mutual responsibility. The early Christians integrated these values into their communal life, thus creating a model of radical sharing.
35.interpretation: This verse shows the importance of community in Christian life, where believers are called to care for one another. It emphasizes that faith is manifested not only through beliefs but also through concrete actions of generosity and mutual support.
35.commentaire: The passage reminds us that true Christian community is built on sharing and mutual aid. By laying their goods at the apostles' feet, believers express their trust in God and in the spiritual leadership of the Church. We are also called to respond to the needs of those around us, practicing generosity and solidarity in our daily lives.

mots.sens: The name 'Barnabas' literally means 'son of encouragement'. This term evokes a person who encourages and supports others in their faith. As a Levite, he is also associated with religious service, which reinforces his role as a supporter within the Christian community. Spiritually, this name highlights the importance of encouragement in the life of the Church, reminding us that every member has a role to play in building up others.

The term 'Levite' designates a person belonging to the tribe of Levi, who had a specific role in temple service and worship. The Levites were responsible for music, teaching the law, and administering sacred rites. In the context of Barnabas, this underscores his commitment to serving God and his supportive role in the Christian community, which is essential for the spiritual growth of the Church.

This word means 'exhortation' or 'consolation', and it is related to the idea of encouraging and comforting others. In the biblical context, this implies moral and spiritual support, essential for strengthening the faith of believers. Exhortation is a fundamental aspect of Christian life, as it helps build strong relationships and fosters spiritual growth within the community.

36.epoque: The book of Acts was written in the first century, at a time when the nascent Christian Church faced persecution and internal and external challenges.
36.passage: This passage is set in a context where the apostles begin to establish the Church in Jerusalem. Barnabas is presented as an example of support and encouragement within this expanding community.
36.culture: In Jewish culture, the Levites had a sacred role and were respected for their service. The idea of exhortation was also valued, as it contributed to maintaining harmony and faith among the people.
36.interpretation: Barnabas, as the 'son of encouragement', represents a model of support and encouragement in Christian life. His role underscores the importance of building strong relationships within the Church and encouraging others in their walk with Christ.
36.commentaire: This verse reminds us that every believer has a precious role to play in building up the Christian community. By being 'Barnabases' for others, we can encourage, support, and strengthen the faith of those around us. Let us be attentive to the call to exhort and encourage, for this is how we contribute to the growth of the Church and the glory of God.

mots.sens: This word means 'field' or 'cultivated land.' It evokes not only a physical space but also the notion of production and harvest. In a spiritual context, it can symbolize generosity and self-giving, representing the willingness to share the blessings received from God. By selling his field, the individual demonstrates a detachment from material possessions in favor of the Christian community.

This term refers to 'money' or 'wealth.' It is often associated with material resources and the management of goods. In this verse, bringing money to the apostles highlights the importance of solidarity and financial support within the Church. It underscores the responsibility of believers to contribute to God's work through material means.

This word means 'feet' and symbolizes humility and respect. By laying the money at the apostles' feet, the individual expresses submission to spiritual authority and a willingness to serve the community. It also illustrates the act of devotion and sacrifice, placing resources at the service of the Church.

37.epoque: This passage is set in the first century AD, during the early days of the Christian Church, when believers shared their possessions to support the community. It was a time of persecution and need, where solidarity was essential for the survival of the Christian faith.
37.passage: Acts 4 describes the growth of the Church after the resurrection of Jesus, highlighting the generosity of the early believers. This verse emphasizes the commitment of the disciples to live in community, sharing their resources for the good of all.
37.culture: In the Jewish culture of the time, sharing goods and mutual aid were fundamental values. Selling properties to support the Christian community reflected a new way of living out faith, where material possessions were considered secondary to spiritual and communal needs.
37.interpretation: This verse illustrates the spirit of generosity that animated the early Christians. By selling his field and bringing the money to the apostles, the believer demonstrates that faith is manifested through concrete actions of support and brotherly love, highlighting the priority of spiritual values over material possessions.
37.commentaire: The act of this man calls us to reflect on our own relationship with material goods. Are we willing to share what we have for the good of the community and for the advancement of the Gospel? This passage encourages us to live an active faith, where our resources are put at the service of God and others, thus illustrating Christian love in concrete acts.
